author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Portuguese digital-rights group D3 has filed collective lawsuits against Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, alleging that platform features are designed to keep users engaged in harmful ways.

The four actions were filed in Lisbon Civil Court between April and May and disclosed after Portugal’s judicial summer break, D3 said Thursday. Collective actions allow an association to bring claims on behalf of a wider group of consumers.

D3 identified infinite scrolling, autoplay video, persistent notifications and highly personalized recommendations as features that remove natural stopping points and repeatedly draw users back. The group is seeking accountability and changes it says would create a safer experience.

Meta, ByteDance and Alphabet, the companies behind the named services, did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment. The allegations have not been adjudicated. The cases join broader scrutiny of social-media design in Europe and the United States, including regulatory proceedings and civil claims concerning compulsive use. D3 said the four platforms together reached 33 million monthly users in Portugal during the first half of 2026, based on data aggregated by SocialMediaTransparency.org. The lawsuits now move into a court process that will test both the group’s claims and the companies’ defenses.
dek: Digital-rights organization D3 says infinite scrolling, autoplay and personalized recommendations create harmful feedback loops.
headline: Portuguese group sues Meta, TikTok and YouTube over addictive design
